sources.title: Current original fence CPU helper run

claims.statement: Each output feature is a weighted sum of input features plus its own additive bias; weight and bias are adjustable parameters.
claims.scope: Linear means PyTorch's affine layer here, explicitly including bias; shared formulas mix numeric input features but do not establish learned semantics.

evidence.supports: The official formula y=xA^T+b identifies one row of learnable weight and one bias per output feature; supports both the recipe interpretation and parameter terminology.
The actual installed implementation preserves the same formula and Parameter shapes.

claims.scope: Two hand-selected dimensionless output features in one sample, not probabilities or performance metrics.

evidence.supports: Independent scalar sums give 10 and 2; derivative with respect to W[0,2] is input feature 4, giving +4 to output 0 only.
Original and perturbed output arrays are exactly equal to independent expected tensors.

verification.expected: [[10,2]] initially; [[14,2]] after one multiplier change; output delta [[4,0]].
verification.observed: Exactly those arrays; manual-vs-forward max absolute error 0.0.
verification.details: CPU float32; one sample, 3 inputs, 2 outputs. Each sum includes one output bias. No denominator or rounding.
verification.tolerance: Exact equality for integer-valued results; original allclose default atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5 also passes.

claims.statement: The original torch tensor/no_grad/copy_/nn.Linear/forward/allclose program sets weight[2,3] and bias[2], then computes the same y as x@weight.T+bias.
claims.scope: Only manual parameter assignment and forward computation in this original fence; default bias=True.

evidence.supports: Constructor arguments, shapes, learnable parameters and forward API match nn.Linear(3,2).
copy_ copies values into the layer tensors; source tensors have exactly matching shapes.
Manual writes occur in a no-grad context which restores gradient recording afterward.
The assertion checks the explicit matrix product elementwise with documented tolerances.
The unmodified fence executes successfully on installed CPU torch and prints expected weight shape and output.

verification.observed: Original helper exits 0 with one fence executed; prints torch.Size([2,3]) and [[10.,2.]]; independent probe confirms shapes and zero error.
verification.details: Helper contract and notebook bootstrap read before execution; no audit guard events. Official original API source v2.9.0 is distinct from installed torch 2.14.1+cpu; installed class/docs and actual operation checked separately.

claims.statement: Linear preserves leading batch/position dimensions and transforms only the last feature axis: [2,4,3] -> [2,4,2]; context mixing requires first flattening each sample to C*D inputs without mixing samples.
claims.scope: C and D are positions and feature width, with fixed linear in_features=C*D; actual ContextMLP implements this preparation.

evidence.supports: All dimensions before the final axis remain the same; only Hin becomes Hout.
Actual implementation uses hidden Linear(context*width,width) and embedding(contexts).flatten(1), retaining the batch axis.
Independent scalar sums match all eight feature rows; one selected input perturbation changes just one output at that same batch/position; actual ContextMLP forward equals its inspected expansion.

verification.expected: Rank3 output shape [2,4,2]; input [0,2,1] +=5 changes only output [0,2,1] by -5. ContextMLP flattens [2,3,2] to [2,6], uses hidden weight [2,6].
verification.observed: All expected shapes and independent values match exactly; no changes in other positions or the other sample; actual repository hidden outputs [[7,10],[5,30]].
verification.details: Rank3 eight input rows are checked against independently constructed scalar formulas. Two ContextMLP samples test preservation of ordering and sample isolation; no training or model-quality measurement.

claims.statement: Transposing the 2D weight changes [2,3] to [3,2] for x[1,3] matrix multiplication; omitting T raises on this non-square example but can silently compute different values with square weights.
claims.scope: T is used on a 2D weight matrix only; silent-error example uses nonsymmetric square W.

evidence.supports: T reverses dimensions, so this 2D weight swaps rows and columns. No higher-dimensional T usage is claimed.
Matrix product contracts imply the needed matching inner dimensions.
Independent products give [7,10] with transpose and [5,11] without it.
Actual untransposed [1,3]@[2,3] raises RuntimeError; the square counterexample executes both products and verifies different results.

verification.expected: Non-square omission fails; for x=[1,2], W=[[1,3],[2,4]], x@W.T=[7,10], x@W=[5,11].
verification.observed: RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (1x3 and 2x3); square results exactly [7,10] and [5,11].
verification.details: The shapes and arithmetic are independently chosen to show both failure modes; square case is nonsymmetric so a mistaken transpose cannot be concealed.

claims.statement: Training can update the learnable weight and bias from a loss gradient; this original example manually sets them and performs no learning or capability evaluation.
claims.scope: The independent single SGD step demonstrates adjustability only; the original fence does not call backward or any optimizer and its grad_fn is not training evidence.

evidence.supports: Official original API declares both weight and bias learnable.
Parameters are updated from objective gradients by theta-lr*gradient in this isolated default SGD setting.
Every original operation is manual assignment, forward calculation or comparison; no backward, optimizer or evaluation code exists.
After the original forward, both gradients remain None and parameters unchanged. A separate one-step loss gives known gradients for both parameters and the expected updates.

verification.expected: Original weight/bias unchanged and grad=None. Separate loss=(10^2+2^2)/2=52; grad W=[[10,20,40],[2,4,8]], grad b=[10,2]; SGD lr=.01 updates both.
verification.observed: Original conditions hold; separate gradients exactly equal those values and resulting W/b equal the independent update within atol=1e-6.
verification.details: Separate one-sample, two-output squared-loss mean has denominator 2; one isolated CPU optimizer step, not a reproduction of model training or an evaluation score. Numeric update tolerance rtol=0, atol=1e-6.

factual_accuracy.details: All substantive mechanisms checked: affine weighted recipes, adjustable parameters, original API behavior, shapes/axes, context flattening, transpose warnings and example-vs-training scope. No unresolved substantive claim found.

numeric_verification.details: Own sums and delta verified against unmodified CPU original and single-weight variation. Dimensionless manual numbers; no averaging or evaluation denominator; exact float32 integer outputs. Additional separate SGD mean denominator 2 is explicitly confined to evidence.
